title: Ashke-Nazis - Blow Up Gaza & New Jerusalem

sense.text:
That’s why we ain’t on nobody’s side. Whose side are we on? God’s side. Always remember that; don’t give a damn about these people.

“And I will set my face against you”: the Lord said he would set his face against us for breaking his laws. “And ye shall be slain before your enemies”: they slew us, as well as the Palestinian Arabs, they been killing us. “They that hate you shall reign over you”: they reign over us, they rule over us. “And ye shall flee when none pursueth you.”

precepts.why:
Let’s go to the New Testament and see what Christ said. “Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted”: there’s coming a time, brothers and sisters, when we will be delivered up into the hands of the American government, based upon the legislation being pushed by the Anti-Defamation League, the Southern Poverty Law Center, the NAACP and so forth, all those different Israeli groups, the Israeli defense project. They’re making laws and legislation saying it’s anti-Semitic to teach the Bible, at least the way we teach it, the correct way, and it will soon be illegal for us to be on the street and teach this word. But Christ warned us about it.

“And shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name’s sake.” There will be a propaganda campaign against us, because we’re trying to liberate the 12 tribes of Israel, and that will be deemed hate speech. We will be imprisoned, some will be put to death. It ain’t a matter of if, it’s a matter of when.

But there is a God, and he has a savior that he has sent for us. “Blessed be the Lord God of Israel”: of who? Of Israel, real Israel, not that fake Israeli state over there. “For he hath visited and redeemed his people”: we are his people. “And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David”: the horn of salvation is the one the world calls Jesus the Christ, and he’s from the house of David. “As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began”: all the prophets from the time of Adam prophesied about the coming Messiah.

“That we should be saved from our enemies”: that’s the purpose of Messiah, to save us from our enemies, “and from the hand of all that hate us.” That’s why we ain’t stressed about the Israelis and we ain’t stressed about the Palestinians. We know they hate us, but God said, I’m going to save you from their hands. “To perform the mercy promised to our fathers, and to remember his holy covenant; The oath which he sware to our father Abraham.”

“That he would grant unto us, that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies might serve him without fear.” The Lord wants us to serve him without fear; right now we serve him in fear. You say you don’t? Yes we do. If you got a job out there and you ain’t working for yourself: Mr. white man, can I have this day off, I got to serve the Lord? No. Can I get Hanukkah? No. Can I get the feast? No, I ain’t got no more days left. That’s called fear. Your wife gets pregnant and you can’t even take days off. You got to pay your taxes, you got to go to work and make this money, so you can’t be there. All kind of fear left and right.

sense.text:
Even their own dictionaries say it: by Edom is meant Rome, and Italy and Greece and all the Western provinces became filled with Idumeans; the prophets call the whole of that nation by the name of Edom. You ain’t going to learn this in church.

“Surely in the fire of my jealousy have I spoken against the residue of the heathen, and against all Idumea.” Idumea is a Greco-Roman name for Edom, E-D-O-M, which means red people, meaning the blood shows through their skin.

“Which have appointed my land into their possession”: these are the people that have taken God’s land, the Holy Land, into their possession. “With the joy of all their heart”: they were happy when they got the land of Israel. “With despiteful minds”: they took the land despite knowing the fact it does not belong to them. “To cast it out for a prey”: that’s how they called their fellow Europeans from Poland, Czechoslovakia, France, Germany, Russia, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, saying come, come, come, and all them rats ran over there.

precepts.why:
“Make a chain: for the land is full of bloody crimes”: this is talking about Israel, the land. “And the city is full of violence”: when we were there our city was full of violence, and this is why we went into slavery.

Now watch what happened as a result: “Wherefore I will bring the worst of the heathen, and they shall possess their houses.” Put them bastards back on the screen; the word mamser means bastards, by the way. Brothers and sisters, I’m not trying to be racist. God said he will bring the worst of the heathen to possess our houses in the land of Israel. God is saying these are the worst; it’s not me saying it, it’s what the Bible says. That look that they have is not our heritage, it’s not biblical.

“I will also make the pomp of the strong to cease; and their holy places shall be defiled”: our holy places have been defiled with these people. But watch what God says: “Destruction cometh; and they shall seek peace, and there shall be none.” There ain’t going to be any.

sense.text:
We read this quite often, but we’re going to keep reading it every Sabbath we can. “And in those times there shall many stand up against the king of the south”: that’s Egypt, the Ptolemy dynasty.

“Also the robbers of thy people”: this is the part we want. Put the images on the screen so everybody knows who I’m talking about. These is them. What did they rob? They robbed our identity, our nationality, our heritage, our land, our country. They robbed everything.

“Shall exalt themselves to establish the vision”: to establish the vision that they are the people of God, that they are the Jews, that they are the Israelites. “But they shall fall”: the Bible says they shall fall. These are the Ashke-Nazis.

precepts.why:
Shout out to the dumb, stupid black apologists and urban apologists out there. Jesus Christ called them something else besides the worst of the heathens.

“I know thy works”: Christ speaking to the real Jews. “And tribulation”: all the hell y’all catching. Smyrna was the church he was talking to. “And poverty”: I know you are impoverished people. “(But thou art rich)”, because all the promises to your forefathers pertain to you.

“And I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not”: they ain’t the Jews. Who are they? “But are the synagogue of Satan.” Jesus Christ called them the synagogue of Satan.

Now the clever Christian goes, see, you Israelites, you’re so wrong, that happened thousands of years ago during the time of Smyrna. Jump to chapter 3 and let’s see you worm your way out of this.

“Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews”: they sure do say they’re Jews, “and are not, but do lie.” Jesus Christ called them a bunch of liars. Christ called them the devil; he called them the synagogue of Satan.

“Behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee.” So to my fellow brothers and sisters in Christianity: when did that happen? Did Christ come and make them bow before our feet to prove that he loves us? It never happened in history. This is a prophecy of what is to come. Don’t let these dumb, stupid Christians fool you.

Solomon calls these people this: “We are esteemed of him as counterfeits.” These people are counterfeits. They are not the Jews, they are not the Israelites. You know what a counterfeit is? A fake, a fraud, a phony.

“He abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness”: we ain’t putting no little boxes on our head, we ain’t running around with no prayer shawls, we ain’t diving in that damn Wailing Wall. We abstain from your ways as filthiness.

“He pronounceth the end of the just to be blessed”: our end is just and blessed, according to thus saith the Lord. “And maketh his boast that God is his father”: God is our father. So that’s an example of how they establish the vision.

sense.text:
It wasn’t good enough just to take the identity as the Jews, because people could say, wait a minute, do you speak the language? They needed the language of the Jews to establish themselves and exalt themselves. Ben Yehuda advocated for creating a new Jewish language. All that’s being spoken over there is not Hebrew, brothers and sisters; he created that language. He authored the modern Hebrew dictionary, and in that dictionary it tells you what the word Esau really means: ‘wasted away is he.’ And when the Bible speaks in Psalms and says let Israel rejoice, sing and dance, that ain’t the kind of music the Most High wants to hear. When you hear black people sing, that’s what the Most High wants.

This is why, brothers and sisters, we don’t argue about language. You got camps out there saying if you don’t say the name their way at least 26 times you can’t get the kingdom of heaven, but that’s not in the Bible. Let’s see what God says.

“Therefore wait ye upon me, saith the Lord, until the day that I rise up to the prey: for my determination is to gather the nations”: God’s going to gather the nations, “that I may assemble the kingdoms”: he’s going to assemble all the kingdoms of the world, “to pour upon them mine indignation”: he’s going to destroy them, “even all my fierce anger: for all the earth shall be devoured with the fire of my jealousy.”

“For then”: meaning after he destroys the militaries of the world. “For then will I turn to the people a pure language.” That’s when the Lord’s going to give us the pure language. He gives you the date: after I destroy the nations of the world, I’m going to give you the pure language. So what are you fussing for, what are you fighting for, what are you mad for? Stop making stuff up. Y’all on the street arguing with us about Hebrew, y’all stupid as hell. Leave us alone.

“That they may all call upon the name of the Lord, to serve him with one consent.” He’s going to make sure we all get that language back, calling on the name of the Lord. Right now we ain’t calling on the name of the Lord, especially with one consent. It ain’t happening right now; we are speaking in the languages of our oppressors.

precepts.why:
Which goes with Isaiah. A couple of brothers approached me some time ago: can I come to IUIC and teach Hebrew? No, brother. Can I come to the school and teach y’all Hebrew? Nope.

“For with stammering lips and another tongue will he speak to this people.” So God speaks to us through the English language, Spanish language, Portuguese language, Creole language and so forth. That’s what people don’t understand about it, and it’s right there.

sense.text:
In order to exalt themselves and establish the vision that they’re the Jews, not only did they take our identity, not only did they create a new form of Hebrew, but they stole the land.

“Surely in the fire of my jealousy have I spoken against the residue of the heathen, and against all Idumea, which have appointed my land into their possession with the joy of all their heart, with despiteful minds.” Look at the map’s color code: the green is Palestinian in 1917; in 1948 the light blue is Israelis, that’s Idumea, and look how they started to take the land over; then the red is under Israeli occupation. The light blue is these fake Israelis; they are the real Idumeans.

Even their own books say the Ashkenazi Jews of Germany, Bohemia and Moravia trace their ancestry to Rome. What did we read about Rome before? Scholars said Edom was Rome. And they say some Jewish Khazars artificially adopted the Levite and Cohen titles; Cohen means priest. Some of y’all be believing these people.

If there was no occupation, invasion, mass murder and stealing of homes, lands and property, there would never be a Hamas. The Ashke-Nazis came into Israel in 1948, Hamas was formed in 1987, and Israel funds them. You got an enemy you can’t stand but you can’t just hit him, so you create a boogeyman: give Hamas some weapons, and when they attack us we will run them over and decimate them, and all the world will be on our side.

Israel has dropped the equivalent of a quarter of a nuclear bomb on Gaza, 6,000 bombs in five days. They said, we got to establish us as the Israelites, and we’ll do anything, kill anybody, lie, hide. You going to tell me these babies are Hamas? If that’s not the attributes of a hate group, there is no such thing. Watch what God says about these so-called white folks, starting with America, with Israel right behind him.

“They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man”: what man is it talking about? The white man. “That made the earth to tremble”: they make the earth to tremble. “That did shake kingdoms”: they’re the ones that shake kingdoms with bombs.

“That made the world as a wilderness”: we’re seeing it. Look at the devastation in Gaza; this is what you’re looking at. “And destroyed the cities thereof”: this is the man God is talking about. It’s not a spiritual demon going around doing it, it’s the earthly demon.

“That opened not the house of his prisoners”: they ain’t letting us go. They ain’t letting the house of their prisoners go.

So now people say, why don’t you stand up for the Palestinians? No, we on God’s side.

“No man that warreth”: brothers and sisters, we are at war, and it’s a spiritual war that we’re in. “Entangleth himself with the affairs of this life.” Why? Because prophecies are going to come. Stay out of God’s work. When he’s allowing these nations to devastate and create catastrophes, just move out of God’s way. Remember King Josiah interfered in God’s work and got put to death for it. So we not going out there protesting; we ain’t picking sides.

“That he may please him”: our job is to please him, “who hath chosen him to be a soldier.” The Lord called us to be soldiers. Our job is to please the Lord, and that’s why we got to remove our emotions out of it. You see this devastation going on with the Palestinians and you want to say or do something, but the Lord said, mind your business, gather the Israelites, that’s what I called you to do.

Now I want to ruffle some feathers with the Black Hebrew Israelites, my frenemies.

“For my son Jesus shall be revealed with those that be with him, and they that remain shall rejoice within four hundred years.” This is talking about the time of Rome, when Christ would be on the scene: 400 years from the time of Ezra, who was in the Persian captivity. Christ was born and grew up while the Roman Empire was ruling. That’s when you read about the people rejoicing, Hosanna, Hosanna, when Christ was walking the earth.

“After these years shall my son Christ die”: he was crucified. “And all men that have life”: that’s the apostles, the disciples, and their disciples. All of those men that had the proper understanding of the law, of the scriptures, died.

“And the world shall be turned into the old silence seven days, like as in the former judgments: so that no man shall remain.” That time period goes from after the fall of Rome into the Dark Ages. No man with proper understanding shall remain; that era was called the Dark Ages. One of the last disciples was Polycarp, the disciple of John the Apostle, who died around 155 AD.

precepts.why:
“And I hated Esau”: God says he hates Esau, that’s the Caucasian race. “And laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.” This was the ushering in of those Dark Ages; that is the Dark Ages. That’s when they were pushed up into the Caucasus mountains of Georgia, Russia.

“Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished”: this is when they were impoverished, when they lived in the Caucasus mountains of Georgia, Russia. “But we will return”: what era was that? The Renaissance. “And build the desolate places”: they built the desolate places.

sense.text: “And I saw an angel come down from heaven, having the key of the bottomless pit and a great chain in his hand.” This great chain represents captivity, slavery.

“And he laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil, and Satan, and bound him a thousand years.” This man who’s called the Devil and Satan: remember what we read in Revelation 2:9, those that say they are Jews and are not. Satan is bound for a thousand years.

“And cast him into the bottomless pit”: that’s Europe. Put him back to the Caucasus mountains. We pushing them right back up there in the mountains, and we going to “set a seal upon him”, so that they don’t come out for a thousand years. It’s going to stink like hell up there; everybody going to be real hairy too, ain’t no Gillette razor up there, smell like mayonnaise and baloney and booty. Right now it’s a tourist attraction.

“That he should deceive the nations no more, till the thousand years should be fulfilled: and after that he must be loosed a little season.”

“And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them”: those thrones are the twelve thrones Christ promised the twelve (Matthew 19:28). “And judgment was given unto them”: power was given unto them, the Israelites.

“And I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God”: that’s why we read earlier in Matthew 24, Christ said they shall kill some of you. This has not come yet with us. “And which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands”: that proves this is talking about the last days, the end times. The mark upon their foreheads is their policies; not in their hands means we didn’t support it.

“And they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.” You have Black Hebrew Israelites saying that’s the Dark Ages. That’s not the Dark Ages. It says they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years, who had not worshipped the beast nor his image nor received the mark in their hand: how is that the Dark Ages? It ain’t. We do talk about the Dark Ages quite a bit and show images, but only to show our image; during the Dark Ages we ruled but we were not righteous, we were not reigning with Christ. This has not happened yet.

“But the rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years were finished”: the rest of the dead is the two thirds of our people that’s done away with, according to Zechariah 13:8. They don’t live again till the thousand years are finished.

That is important because there are Black Hebrew Israelites who have taught some of y’all listening online that you can be an adulterer, a liar, a thief, and when you die you come back in the Kingdom as a baby boy. Ain’t no way, boy, you escape judgment. That makes no sense: what I got to repent for then, I could be as wicked as I want, die and be a baby in the Kingdom of Heaven? “This is the first resurrection.”

“Blessed and holy is he that hath part in the first resurrection”: all of us should want part in this first resurrection; that’s when Christ returns. “On such the second death hath no power”: the second death is that final judgment.

“But they shall be priests of God and of Christ”: we’re going to be God. “And shall reign with him a thousand years”: how long? A thousand years, a thousand years of peace. That goes back to verse four.

precepts.why:
Let’s talk about these thrones for a moment. Christ said unto the twelve, “Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of man shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.” You twelve shall sit upon twelve thrones.

There’s going to be rank and order in the Kingdom. Them twelve are going to be over everybody. Those are the thrones John saw in Revelation 20:4, and they that sat upon them.

“For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a king”: we have no king even today. “And without a prince”: we have no prince. “And without a sacrifice”: we have no sacrifice. “And without an image”: that’s the part I wanted. We have no image today; our image has been erased.

So when we talk about the Dark Ages, it’s only to show y’all our images. We only show the images of our people during the Dark Ages to show that we ruled, we were kings and leaders and warriors during that time, but we were not righteous. Remember it said all men that had life died off.

The book ‘Image of the Black in Western Art’, from Harvard; they won’t teach you this in school. St Maurice, a black man, showing that we were the knights of the time: these were the images they had throughout Europe of a black man and black men. St Maurice and his companions, all them black men. They make you think that during the Dark Ages we were nonexistent. No, we ruling; we pushed them white folks up into the caves of the Caucasus mountains. St Maurice was a military leader, legendary over the Theban legion of Rome during the 3rd century: St Maurice and his 6,000 African soldiers, black men. You’ll never see this on TV or in the movies; they’ll show you white folks everywhere. They were ordered to put down a rebellion against the empire, and when St Maurice discovered they were all Christians, he and his men refused to fight their fellow Christians and refused to sacrifice to the Roman god. That’s what got them put to death: the emperor killed St Maurice and all his legion because they didn’t follow his orders.

The earliest surviving work portraying Maurice as a dark complexioned African dates from the 12th century; now we know that he was an Israelite. Then the part I want y’all to see: the black images of him died out in the mid 16th century, undermined by the developing Atlantic slave trade. I wonder why. They didn’t want the slaves to know that we was warriors and saints and leaders. That’s what these damn devils did; that’s why they hide it in the books today. Once again the color black had become associated with spiritual darkness and otherness: he’s evil, he ain’t right. That’s what they did.

Another book: we worshipped Mary during the Dark Ages. She’s in the center of all these images. Icons from the Moscow Kremlin museums, from the 1550s, follow the text of the prayer chanted in honor of the Virgin: we were doing prayers and honoring Mary, the ever virgin, they called her. So this is not us reigning with Christ for a thousand years. These famous images of Mary and baby Christ we only show to show they were black, painted by black people; but this was a time of darkness. When I say darkness, I mean we did not have the truth; we was being wicked.

In case any sister in here wants to honor Mary. “A certain woman of the company lifted up her voice, and said unto him, Blessed is the womb that bare thee”: bless your mama. “And the paps which thou hast sucked”: bless your mama’s titties, that’s what it’s saying.

“But he said, Yea rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it.” So don’t be honoring my mama; you honor the word of God, and you do what it says. That is why worshipping Mary in the Dark Ages was not reigning with Christ.

We were not reigning with Christ a thousand years during the Dark Ages. In the painting called the church militant are many of the famous black soldiers, warriors and leaders. The celestial host is proceeding from the burning citadel of Kazan, which Ivan the Terrible captured from the Tartars in 1552, a mundane city of sin, towards the celestial Jerusalem, where the enthroned Virgin is, Mary, with the infant Jesus on her lap. The Archangel Michael, captain of the heavenly host, is black on horseback, with Ivan the Terrible behind him. The man holding the cross is either Constantine or Vladimir Monomakh, a black man; then Prince Vladimir with his sons Boris and Gleb. These are not Caucasians. We only show these images to show you we were the rulers, we were the leaders; but we weren’t right, we were not right.

Then the white man came against us and slaughtered us, chopping our bodies up, and you see the lion of Judah on the shield. Black men in the castle fighting off white men on horseback; the wildlings from The Game of Thrones, that’s who we were fighting. They overthrew us in Europe because we were not right; we were not reigning with Christ for a thousand years during this time. Obviously we lost the war, because we’re here in America now.

“The earth is given into the hand of the wicked.” Look at the image of Christ, black, a Russian leader black in the background, and a painting over the black image as a white woman or a white man, whatever that is, but Caucasian. That’s what they do. These people have been hired to paint over all the black images, like we read in Wikipedia, so that the slaves would never see this stuff, because this would cause us to unite and uprise. They said don’t show it to the slaves.

And another book: they had white folks pose for the Madonna and child, and the bust of the Savior, found in the church of San Salvatore (Salvatore means savior), was posed for by the son of Pope Alexander the 6th of Rome. It is an open secret, meaning white folks knew all about it but not the slaves. They’re telling you in the book, so we ain’t making it up. This is who all your mamas and papas pray to: Caesar, an Edomite, the devil the Bible speaks of.

Another precept to that one: don’t let the Black Hebrew Israelites fool you. “Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven unto men. And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him”: we were forgiven, all the wicked.

“But whosoever speaketh against the Holy Ghost”: you learn this truth and you reject this truth, “it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world”: you will not be forgiven in this current world, “neither in the world to come”: that’s the Kingdom of Heaven on Earth.

So don’t let Black Hebrew Israelites deceive y’all, running around in these camps saying I can be wicked and I’m going to get the Kingdom. That’s a lie; the devil is a liar. The rest of the dead live not again until the thousand years are finished.

sense.text:
What happens when we reign with Christ. “And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls”: the sons of strangers are the other nations; they’re going to build up our walls. We’re going to have walls on our houses, and the sanctuaries. “And their kings shall minister unto thee.”

“For in my wrath I smote thee”: God’s wrath, he smote us; that’s slavery. “But in my favour have I had mercy on thee.”

“Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that men may bring unto thee”, the Israelite kings and priests, “the forces of the Gentiles”: meaning the wealth of the nations. “And that their kings may be brought”: their kings will be brought as slaves, brought in chains.

“For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish”: any nation that disobeys us shall perish. We going to tell them bow the knee; remember it says every knee shall bow and every tongue shall confess that Jesus Christ is Lord.

“Yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.” I bet you didn’t never read that in church.

“The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together”: all the glory of Lebanon, the trees that come from Lebanon. Why? “To beautify the place of my sanctuary.” Listen good, brothers and sisters: there’s going to be a sanctuary built, just like in the days of old, but more glorious. “And I will make the place of my feet glorious.”

“The sons also of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee”: these nations afflicted us, and they going to come bending unto us, the Israelites, the children of God. “And all they that despised thee”: all they that hated our black lips and our black necks and our black gums, “shall bow themselves down at the soles of thy feet.” They going to bow; that’s every knee shall bow and every tongue confess. That sounds like what we read earlier in Revelation 3:9: the same thing.

This ain’t talking about bowing today. Anybody that kiss your boot today got a sex fetish.

So y’all thought I was making it up when I said bow the knee. Bishop, you just a racist? I’m not racist, I love my race; I’m telling you what thus saith the Lord. “And they shall call thee, The city of the Lord, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel.”

“Whereas thou hast been forsaken”: we were forsaken of all nations; no nation stands by our side. We getting emails and letters saying why don’t you stand up for the Palestinians. The hell with them. Who stands up for us? What nation stands up for our race? “And hated”: God says all nations hate our guts. “So that no man went through thee”: nobody helps us.

“I will make thee an eternal excellency, a joy of many generations.”

“Thou shalt also suck the milk of the Gentiles”: we going to get all their wealth, because it’s our wealth. “And shalt suck the breast of kings”: the kings going to take care of us. “And thou shalt know that I the Lord am thy Saviour and thy Redeemer, the mighty One of Jacob.”

“For brass I will bring gold”: we got little cheap brass rings, brass necklaces; the Lord said don’t worry about that, all the brass you got, I’m going to bring gold to you. Not the cheap 18 karat, 14 karat: the gold of Ophir, the pure gold, real gold, not no cheap plastic. “And for iron I will bring silver, and for wood brass, and for stones iron.”

“I will also make thy officers peace, and thine exactors righteousness”: an exactor is a tax collector. We going to tax the nations every month: bring up your damn taxes.

“Violence shall no more be heard in thy land”: that’s peace on earth, good will toward men, when we ruling. “Wasting nor destruction within thy borders; but thou shalt call thy walls Salvation, and thy gates Praise.”

Write this down: what we read in Isaiah 60 is Revelation 20:4.

precepts.why:
There’s a Christian right now saying you making stuff up. “That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow”: now we know it’s not going to be his name in the Kingdom, because he says in Revelation 3 he has a new name that no man knoweth but he himself. Every knee shall bow, “of things in heaven, and things in earth”, everything on the earth, “and things under the earth.”

“And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.” Every tongue going to confess that Jesus Christ is Lord. That is the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish: they bow the knee and confess, or they perish.

Some of y’all might think everybody’s going to love Jesus. No they not. When Christ return there are going to be rebellious nations on earth. For all you Christians who think when Christ come everybody going to have peace: oh shut up.

“Neither repented they of their murders, nor of their sorceries, nor of their fornication, nor of their thefts.” From verse twenty: “And the rest of the men which were not killed by these plagues”, the rest of the nations that were not killed, “yet repented not”. Brothers and sisters, these nations ain’t going to repent. They’re not going to change.

“That they should not worship devils, and idols of gold, and silver, and brass, and stone, and of wood: which neither can see, nor hear”. When it says wood and stone, that means the Christians ain’t going to repent, or the Muslims, they ain’t repenting; that’s why it says stone. That is why the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish, and those nations shall be utterly wasted.

We just read about the Kingdom; now I’m backing up for a second. “Thus saith the Lord God; Behold, I will take the children of Israel from among the heathen”: right now we still are amongst the heathen. “And will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land”: the Lord is going to bring the twelve tribes of Israel into our own land. That prophecy has not occurred yet.

“And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations”: we will no more be divided into the kingdom of Judah and the kingdom of Israel, the kingdom of Ephraim. “Neither shall they defile themselves any more with their idols”: our idols going to be cast away. “And will cleanse them”: the Lord said he will cleanse us. “So shall they be my people, and I will be their God.”

“And David my servant shall be king over them”: amongst the twelve, because they going to be the top, David is amongst the twelve. If you don’t know who David is amongst the twelve, shame on you. “And they all shall have one shepherd: they shall also walk in my judgments, and observe my statutes, and do them”: we’re going to observe and do God’s laws. “And they shall dwell in the land that I have given unto Jacob my servant”: we going to dwell in our land, “even they, and their children, and their children’s children for ever”: there’s going to be generations, forever. “And my servant David shall be their prince for ever.”

“Moreover I will make a covenant of peace with them; it shall be an everlasting covenant with them: and I will place them, and multiply them, and will set my sanctuary in the midst of them for evermore.” He’s going to set a sanctuary in the midst of us forever. “My tabernacle also shall be with them”, and the heathen, all the other nations, “shall know that I the Lord do sanctify Israel, when my sanctuary shall be in the midst of them for evermore.” That sanctuary is what we read in Isaiah 60: the place of my sanctuary. It’s saying the same thing.

sense.text: “And when the thousand years are expired”: after the thousand years of us reigning with Christ, the thousand years of peace, “Satan shall be loosed out of his prison.” That’s Ezekiel 38.

“And shall go out to deceive the nations which are in the four quarters of the earth, Gog and Magog, to gather them together to battle: the number of whom is as the sand of the sea.” After the thousand-year reign the Lord’s going to say release those nations that were bound. It’s going to be time for them to organize themselves; they going to get weapons, and they going to think they going to come after us.
“And they went up on the breadth of the earth, and compassed the camp of the saints about, and the beloved city: and fire came down from God out of heaven, and devoured them.”

“And the devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet are”: the beast, that’s the seven heads and ten horns, and the false prophet, that’s the church system. So by then America’s already destroyed, the church system destroyed. “And shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever.”

Ezekiel 37 ends with God’s tabernacle with us and the heathen knowing that he sanctifies Israel, and it goes right into chapter 38: “Son of man, set thy face against Gog, the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, and prophesy against him”. What I’m showing you from Ezekiel 37 and 38 is the same thing as Revelation 20 verses 4 through 9; it’s going in the same order. First the Kingdom, then Gog and Magog.

“And I will turn thee back, and put hooks into thy jaws, and I will bring thee forth, and all thine army, horses and horsemen, all of them clothed with all sorts of armour”, “Persia, Ethiopia, and Libya with them”, “Gomer, and all his bands; the house of Togarmah of the north quarters”: these are the nations gathered to battle, “Be thou prepared, and prepare for thyself”.

“After many days thou shalt be visited”: you see that part right there. That is the same as Revelation 20, where they shall be loosed after the thousand years.

“In the latter years thou shalt come into the land that is brought back from the sword, and is gathered out of many people, against the mountains of Israel”: it’s telling you Israel is brought back from the sword and gathered out of many people. How would you think that’s talking about the people over there today? “Which have been always waste”: if you go to Israel today (we’ve been to Israel), it’s a wasteland, the whole place like a desert. The trees are flown in, the grass is brought in; it’s all artificial.

“But it is brought forth out of the nations”: true Israel is brought forth out of the nations. “And they shall dwell safely all of them”: are they dwelling safely over there? No. So this is talking about us.
“Thou shalt ascend and come like a storm”: Gog and Magog and the nations shall ascend and come like a storm, “thou shalt be like a cloud to cover the land”.
“At the same time shall things come into thy mind, and thou shalt think an evil thought”. What’s the evil thought?

“And thou shalt say, I will go up to the land of unwalled villages”. Wait a minute: we just read in Isaiah 60 about walls, and I said we going to have walls on our homes and a tabernacle. Unwalled villages is us in the Kingdom (Zechariah 2), and the walls are the sanctuary and Jerusalem, with the rest of Israel dwelling all around it, the same way it was in the days of the tabernacle and the temple.

precepts.why:
The proper precept for after many days thou shalt be visited, where they shall be loosed. “And cast him into the bottomless pit, and shut him up, and set a seal upon him, that he should deceive the nations no more, till the thousand years should be fulfilled”: “and after that he must be loosed a little season.”

Then verse seven: “And when the thousand years are expired, Satan shall be loosed out of his prison, And shall go out to deceive the nations which are in the four quarters of the earth, Gog and Magog, to gather them together to battle: the number of whom is as the sand of the sea.” Ezekiel saying after many days thou shalt be visited is Satan loosed when the thousand years are expired.

Another precept about them being loosed. “And they shall be gathered together, as prisoners are gathered in the pit”: talking about the white man, the bottomless pit of Revelation 20. “And shall be shut up in the prison”: that’s that seal and that great chain.

“And after many days shall they be visited”: the same words as Ezekiel 38:8. After many days they shall be visited, meaning loosed.

A precept for they shall dwell safely all of them, talking about us. “In those days shall Judah be saved, and Jerusalem shall dwell safely: and this is the name wherewith she shall be called, The Lord our righteousness.”

When we’re in the land, it says prophetically we shall dwell safely. So the bottom of Ezekiel 38:8, “and they shall dwell safely all of them”, is talking about us, not them over there today.

It said unwalled villages, and I said that’s us in the Kingdom. “Behold a man with a measuring line in his hand.” “To measure Jerusalem, to see what is the breadth thereof, and what is the length thereof”: he wants to know the size.

“And, behold, the angel that talked with me went forth, and another angel went out to meet him, And said unto him, Run, speak to this young man, saying, Jerusalem shall be inhabited as towns without walls”, safely. I want you to understand that, so you know I’m not delirious; I didn’t lose my mind; I know what I’m talking about. “For the multitude of men and cattle therein”.

“For I, saith the Lord, will be unto her a wall of fire round about, and will be the glory in the midst of her.” The Lord is going to be unto us a wall of fire round about, and the glory in the midst of us. That is the land of unwalled villages Gog will go up against.

Somebody saying the Bishop don’t know what he talking about, we got scripture that says we going to have walls: shut up, just be quiet. “Then verily the first covenant had also ordinances of divine service, and a worldly sanctuary. For there was a tabernacle made; the first, wherein was the candlestick, and the table, and the shewbread; which is called the sanctuary. And after the second veil, the tabernacle which is called the Holiest of all”. During the time of Moses we had the tabernacle, and inside it was the holy of holies, which only the high priest went into, with the ark of the covenant; sacrifices were done out in the center. That is how in Exodus you read about the tabernacle.

“And over it the cherubims of glory shadowing the mercyseat; of which we cannot now speak particularly.” Paul says we cannot now speak particularly because it would symbolize something: it symbolizes the Lord on his throne, with those two huge angels over the throne.

“The priests went always into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the service of God”: the priest was only allowed to go into the first tabernacle. “But into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood”: we know who the high priest is today, Christ. “The Holy Ghost this signifying, that the way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest”: it wasn’t made manifest during the time of Moses, “while as the first tabernacle was yet standing: Which was a figure for the time then present”. That word figure means a symbol, a representation, or a shadow.

In the pictures you see the tabernacle with the holy of holies, where the spirit of the Lord would come down and talk with Aaron and Moses, and Israel all around it. After Moses, Solomon built the temple, which was the tabernacle built in gold and mortar and brick; it represented the first tabernacle Moses had set up. That was burned down; we rebuilt it during the Persian captivity; then Herod added to it. Same thing: inside, the holy of holies, only the high priest went in there; the priests in the courtyard; and the homes and houses of Israel all around it. All of Israel did not live in Jerusalem, only some of Judah and Benjamin, and some Levi; the rest of Israel lived all around it. It’s going to be the same way in Isaiah 60: redone the same way, on a larger and more beautiful scale.

“And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls, and their kings shall minister unto thee”. “Therefore thy gates shall be open continually”: this is the reconstruction, the rebuilding of Jerusalem. “That men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles”: the nations bring their wealth, “and that their kings may be brought”, in chains.

“The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary”: that sanctuary is going to be built just like in the days of old, but more glorious. “And I will make the place of my feet glorious.” So Jerusalem and the sanctuary have walls, and Israel dwells round about it in the land of unwalled villages, with the Lord a wall of fire round about.

sense.text: The party ain’t over. “For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth: and the former shall not be remembered, nor come into mind.” “For, behold, I create Jerusalem a rejoicing, and her people a joy.”
“And the voice of weeping shall be no more heard in her, nor the voice of crying.” This is what we read in Isaiah 60, and this is Revelation 20:4.

“There shall be no more thence an infant of days”: meaning no more stillbirths, stillborns and premature births. “Nor an old man that hath not filled his days: for the child shall die an hundred years old”.

In the Kingdom are we going to be dropping dead? No. We’re going to be immortal, and Israel shall be all righteous (Isaiah 60:21). So this ain’t talking about us. “But the sinner being an hundred years old shall be accursed”: are we going to be sinners? We going to be all righteous. This is the nations.

“And they shall build houses, and inhabit them; and they shall plant vineyards, and eat the fruit of them.” Who’s going to be planting and doing all of this? The nations. “They shall not build, and another inhabit; they shall not plant, and another eat: for as the days of a tree are the days of my people”: we want to live long. “And mine elect shall long enjoy the work of their hands.”
“They shall not labour in vain, nor bring forth for trouble; for they are the seed of the blessed of the Lord, and their offspring with them.”

“And it shall come to pass, that before they call”, before we send our prayer, “I will answer”: the Lord said I will answer. “And while they are yet speaking”, while we yet speaking in our prayer, “I will hear.”

“The wolf and the lamb shall feed together, and the lion shall eat straw like the bullock: and dust shall be the serpent’s meat. They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain, saith the Lord.” That’s Isaiah 60; that’s Revelation 20:4.

precepts.why:
Hold Isaiah 65 and get Isaiah 60:21. “Thy people also shall be all righteous”: all Israel is going to be righteous.

So when we go back to Isaiah 65:20, the child dying an hundred years old and the sinner being accursed is not talking about us. We will be immortal and all righteous; it’s the nations that die and the sinner that is accursed.

Why would the other nations live so long? Everything’s going to be on another level, brothers and sisters. “In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits”: that goes to the twelve tribes of Israel. “And yielded her fruit every month”: every month there’s going to be some understanding that comes out.

“And the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.” If the nations obey, they going to live. That’s why we read in Isaiah 65 that there shall be no more an infant of days, and the child shall die an hundred years old.

A quick precept on the nations obeying. “And it shall come to pass, that every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles”: everybody going to obey God’s laws.

“And it shall be, that whoso will not come up of all the families of the earth unto Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, even upon them shall be no rain”: that means they’re going to die. That’s what we were just reading in Isaiah 65 about them dying an hundred years old. If they obey, they’re going to live a little longer.

“And if the family of Egypt go not up”: if Egypt decide we ain’t going up, “and come not, that have no rain”, they going to have a famine, a drought, and die. “There shall be the plague, wherewith the Lord will smite the heathen that come not up to keep the feast of tabernacles.” If the nations will not obey, there’s going to be plagues on them; they’re going to die.

sense.text: “But in the last days it shall come to pass, that the mountain of the house of the Lord shall be established in the top of the mountains”: this is Revelation 20:4, this is Isaiah 60, this is Isaiah 65, this is Zechariah 2:1-5. “And it shall be exalted above the hills; and people shall flow unto it.”

“And many nations shall come, and say, Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for the law shall go forth of Zion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.”

“And he shall judge among many people, and rebuke strong nations afar off”: we got to subdue the nations. “And they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks”: that’s going to be peace, world peace, for a thousand years. “Nation shall not lift up a sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more”: that’s world peace, brothers and sisters, only when Christ and the twelve tribes are established.

“But they shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and none shall make them afraid”: we going to dwell safely; that’s what we were just reading in Ezekiel 38. “For the mouth of the Lord of hosts hath spoken it.”

“For all people will walk every one in the name of his god”: the god they going to walk in the name of is us (Psalms 82:6; Zechariah 12:8). “And we will walk in the name of the Lord our God for ever and ever.”

precepts.why:
Hold that: the name of his god. This is the god they going to walk in. “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.”

That goes with Luke 19, where Christ said well done, thou good and faithful servant, be thou lord over ten cities; be thou lord over five cities. You going to be God to those nations. We going to be God to the nations.

Don’t play with us. “In that day shall the Lord defend the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and he that is feeble among them at that day shall be as David; and the house of David shall be as God”. As what? As God. That’s what Micah 4:5 is talking about: all people will walk every one in the name of his god.

sense.text:
I’m still showing you the correlation; y’all online, y’all Black Hebrew Israelites, get mad if you want, I don’t care. On this side we rejoicing. This is about Gog and Magog. “And thou shalt say, I will go up to the land of unwalled villages”: what did we read in Zechariah 2? We would be as towns without walls.

“I will go to them that are at rest”: we at rest. Remember Christ said come unto me all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. “That dwell safely, all of them dwelling without walls”: that goes back to Zechariah 2:4. “And having neither bars nor gates”.

“To take a spoil, and to take a prey”: they want to rob us. “Upon the people that are gathered out of the nations, which have gotten cattle and goods”: we have gotten cattle and goods. Remember what we read in Isaiah 60: they going to bring their wealth, the forces of the Gentiles.

“Sheba, and Dedan, and the merchants of Tarshish, with all the young lions thereof, shall say unto thee, Art thou come to take a spoil?” They going to say to Gog, you going up there to rob them? “To carry away silver and gold”: why does it say to carry away silver and gold? Because that’s what we going to have, silver and gold. “To take away cattle and goods, to take a great spoil?”
“In that day when my people of Israel dwelleth safely”: this is not the Edomites, brothers; this is the Israelites.

“And thou shalt come from thy place out of the north parts, thou, and many people with thee, all of them riding upon horses, a great company, and a mighty army: And thou shalt come up against my people of Israel, as a cloud to cover the land; it shall be in the latter days, and I will bring thee against my land, that the heathen may know me”.
“Art thou he of whom I have spoken in old time by my servants the prophets of Israel”: like Ezekiel, “which prophesied in those days many years that I would bring thee against them?”

“When Gog shall come against the land of Israel, saith the Lord God, that my fury shall come up in my face.” “Surely in that day there shall be a great shaking in the land of Israel”: the fishes, the fowls, the beasts and “all the men that are upon the face of the earth, shall shake at my presence”. They going to shake at the presence of the Lord. “And the mountains shall be thrown down, and the steep places shall fall, and every wall shall fall to the ground.”

“Every man’s sword shall be against his brother. And I will plead against him with pestilence and with blood; and I will rain upon him, and upon his bands, and upon the many people that are with him, an overflowing rain, and great hailstones, fire, and brimstone.” You see that fire and brimstone: that’s the same as Revelation 20, fire came down from God out of heaven. Stop listening to Christians.
“Thus will I magnify myself, and sanctify myself; and I will be known in the eyes of many nations, and they shall know that I am the Lord.”

precepts.why: “And said unto him, Run, speak to this young man, saying, Jerusalem shall be inhabited as towns without walls”. There you go: that is the land of unwalled villages Gog says he will go up to, Israel dwelling safely in the Kingdom, all of them dwelling without walls.

Ezekiel’s fire and brimstone is the part in Revelation 20 where fire came down from heaven; it’s saying the same thing. “And they went up on the breadth of the earth, and compassed the camp of the saints about, and the beloved city: and fire came down from God out of heaven, and devoured them. And the devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet are”.

The great hailstones, fire and brimstone that God rains upon Gog and all his bands is the fire that came down from God out of heaven when Gog and Magog compassed the camp of the saints after the thousand years.

sense.text: It ain’t over: the war on Gog continues in chapter 39. “Behold, I am against thee, O Gog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal: And I will turn thee back, and leave but the sixth part of thee.” The Lord says he will leave but the sixth part of them, and he brings them “upon the mountains of Israel” to fall there.

“Thou shalt fall upon the mountains of Israel, thou, and all thy bands”, given “unto the ravenous birds of every sort, and to the beasts of the field to be devoured.” The Lord sends “a fire on Magog”, and makes his holy name known “in the midst of my people Israel”, and will not let them pollute his holy name any more. “Behold, it is come, and it is done, saith the Lord God; this is the day whereof I have spoken.”

“And they that dwell in the cities of Israel shall go forth, and shall set on fire and burn the weapons”: the shields, the bucklers, the bows, the arrows, the handstaves and the spears, “and they shall burn them with fire seven years.” How long? Seven years. We are going to burn their weapons for seven years.
“They shall spoil those that spoiled them, and rob those that robbed them, saith the Lord God.” We are going to spoil them that robbed us.

God gives Gog a place of graves in Israel, “the valley of the passengers on the east of the sea: and it shall stop the noses of the passengers.” Meaning it is going to smell so bad, the way you hold your nose.

“Seven months shall the house of Israel be burying of them, that they may cleanse the land.” How are you going to read all this and say that is talking about them over there in Israel? It ain’t talking about them over there. This is the house of Israel, the true Israelites, burying the multitude that came against them.

“They shall sever out men of continual employment, passing through the land to bury”: there is always going to be a job, continual employment, burying with the passengers “those that remain upon the face of the earth, to cleanse it.” When any “seeth a man’s bone, then shall he set up a sign by it, till the buriers have buried it in the valley of Hamon–gog”, and “Thus shall they cleanse the land.” And the party ain’t over: from here the class goes right back to Revelation 20.

Pay close attention. In verse 4 we reigned for a thousand years. After the thousand years, who is released and who comes up against us? The ones just read in Ezekiel 38 and 39. Now verse 11: “I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away.” The one on that throne is Christ, the one who destroys death (1 Corinthians 15).
“The dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.” Their works means whether they kept God’s law or did not keep God’s law.

“The sea gave up the dead which were in it”: all those that died in the sea, their souls shall come up. That is a metaphor, because there is a place where they all dwell. “And death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them: and they were judged every man according to their works.”
“And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death.” The second death is that final judgment, and after that final judgment death and hell is no more.

“And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.” Wait a minute, so who is that? All the other nations. Israel is written in the book (Daniel 12:1); the multitude of the nations was born in vain (2 Esdras 9:22). So all the other nations that y’all are so enamored by are going to have an end.

precepts.why:
To see who is written in the Lamb’s book of life: “at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people”, the children of thy people being the Israelites. “And at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.”

So who is written in the book? The children of Israel. Whoever is not found written there, in Revelation 20:15, is the other nations.

What about the other nations? “Let the multitude perish then, which was born in vain; and let my grape be kept, and my plant; for with great labour have I made it perfect.” The grape and the plant that are kept are us, the elect.

Read the first part again: “Let the multitude perish then, which was born in vain.” The multitude of the nations was born in vain. They are the ones not written in the book of life and cast into the lake of fire.

Your church never showed y’all this, not ‘my Jesus, he love everybody’. “Fear thou not, O Jacob my servant, saith the Lord: for I am with thee; for I will make a full end of all the nations whither I have driven thee: but I will not make a full end of thee.”

He will make a full end of all the nations, but he will not make a full end of the Israelites, meaning we are still going to be around. The nations, brothers and sisters, the ones some of y’all chase after and find so attractive: God says I am going to make a full end of them. Let the multitude perish; they were born in vain. That is Revelation 20:14-15: death and hell cast into the lake of fire, and whosoever was not found written in the book of life cast in with them.

“Then cometh the end, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Father.” Write this down: that he is Christ. Christ delivers up the kingdom to the Father “when he shall have put down all rule and all authority and power.” World dominion: Christ is going to make sure everyone is subdued. “For he must reign, till he hath put all enemies under his feet”, under Christ’s feet.

“The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death.” That is Revelation 20:14, death and hell cast into the lake of fire. So who is the one destroying death? It is Christ. So in Revelation 20 that is Christ; he is the one on the throne.

Then read it slow and watch every he. “For he hath put all things under his feet”: that he is the Father, putting all things under Christ’s feet. “But when he saith all things are put under him”: when the Father saith all things are put under Christ, “it is manifest that he is excepted, which did put all things under him”, meaning except the Father. The Father is not going under Christ’s feet.

“And when all things shall be subdued unto him, then shall the Son also himself be subject unto him that put all things under him, that God may be all in all.” Christ is subject unto the Father. So what happens next? That is the question, and Revelation 21 answers it.

sense.text:
This is what happens after. Remember chapter 20: what happened to the nations? They are gone, judged by Christ and cast into the lake of fire. Now in chapter 21 John sees “a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away; and there was no more sea.” No more sea means the nations are gone, for the multitude of many people make a noise like the noise of the seas (Isaiah 17:12).

Revelation 21:1-23 is after the thousand year reign, after the second death. That is the cube, the city that goes up to space.
“And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.” John sees the holy city coming down.

“Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people”: Israel is the people. “And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying.”

“Behold, I make all things new.” These words are true and faithful. “I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end”: this is Christ, who gives “unto him that is athirst of the fountain of the water of life freely.” “He that overcometh shall inherit all things; and I will be his God, and he shall be my son.”

“But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death.” He is telling you what happened in chapter 20, verses 14 and 15.

So, brothers, we cannot be fearful in this truth. You cannot be unbelieving in this truth; some of you are here and your faith is weak, so pray for more faith, like Peter asked the Lord to increase our faith. Murderers: if you got that hateful, murderous spirit on you. Whoremongers: that’s you brothers, y’all know who you are, jumping around from person to person. Sorcerers: you’re all into horoscopes and witchcraft and juju. Idolaters: you put anything above the Lord, whether it’s money, an actual idol, or your job. And all liars. All of them have their part in the lake of fire, which goes back to the previous chapter.

One of the seven angels says, “Come hither, I will shew thee the bride, the Lamb’s wife”, and shows John “that great city, the holy Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from God, Having the glory of God.” I am going to show you this great city which descends out of heaven from God.

Listen: it “had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel.” Three gates on the east, three on the north, three on the south, three on the west. And the wall had twelve foundations, “and in them the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.”

He has a golden reed to measure the city, the gates and the wall. Pay close attention: “the city lieth foursquare”, a perfect square, and length, breadth and height are all equal. “He measured the city with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs”: 1,500 miles. Everything is equal on this city.

How high is the edge of space from the earth? 62 miles. If it is 62 miles to get from the earth to space, the Bible says this city is 1,500 miles, 1,500 miles cubed. That is out in space.

Isaiah 60 and Revelation 21 are two different things. In Isaiah 60 the nations build our walls; the nations cannot go into space and build this. This is two different kingdoms. And is this the city Gog and Magog try to take down? No, this ain’t the same thing. They cannot get there; it is 1,500 miles up to space. It is finished at this point. Everybody’s gone; the nations are done, they are gone already.

“He measured the wall thereof, an hundred and forty and four cubits, according to the measure of a man”: by a man’s measure that would be 216 feet. But notice: “that is, of the angel.” This is not measured on a man, it is based on the size of an angel, and an angel ain’t our size; an angel is huge. So why is this city so big? Because the heaven is God’s throne and the earth his footstool (Isaiah 66:1).

“The building of the wall of it was of jasper: and the city was pure gold, like unto clear glass.” The city is pure gold. All these stones of the foundations are the same stones the high priest wore in the time of Moses, on the ephod. “The street of the city was pure gold, as it were transparent glass”: we can’t even comprehend that.

This is very important. “And I saw no temple therein.” That lets us know for sure this is different from Isaiah 60, where they shall beautify the place of God’s sanctuary. Remember the tabernacle of Moses and the temple Solomon built. In this city there is going to be no temple, “for the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are the temple of it.” The Father and the Son are going to be the temple.
“The city had no need of the sun, neither of the moon, to shine in it: for the glory of God did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof.”

Listen: from verse 24 all the way down through chapter 22 is a recap of Revelation chapter 20 and Isaiah 60, giving a summary again. “And the nations of them which are saved shall walk in the light of it: and the kings of the earth do bring their glory and honour into it.” Whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire (Revelation 20:15), so there are no nations when the kingdom of verses 1 to 23 comes from heaven. When nations show up at verse 24, it is recapping.

Write it down: Revelation 21:24-27, all the way through Revelation 22, is a recap or summary of Revelation 20:1-6. Isaiah 60 is explaining Revelation 20; Micah 4 is explaining Revelation 20; Isaiah 2 is explaining Revelation 20, the reigning with Christ; Zechariah 14, about the nations coming up, and Zechariah 2:1-5 go with it too. Revelation 21:1-23 is after the thousand year reign, after the second death.

“The gates of it shall not be shut at all by day”, “And they shall bring the glory and honour of the nations into it”: the same thing Isaiah 60 says. “And there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth, neither whatsoever worketh abomination, or maketh a lie: but they which are written in the Lamb’s book of life.” So only Israel is going to be able to enter the temple, the sanctuary. This is based on Isaiah 60 and Revelation 20, not on Revelation 21:1-23. Two different things.

precepts.why: This is what “there was no more sea” means: “Woe to the multitude of many people, which make a noise like the noise of the seas.” The sea is the multitude of the nations. When John sees a new heaven and a new earth with no more sea, the nations are gone.

Jump back to chapter 20: “And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death.” Revelation 21:8 is telling you what happened in chapter 20. The fearful, the unbelieving, the abominable, the murderers, whoremongers, sorcerers, idolaters and all liars have their part in that same lake which burneth with fire and brimstone, the second death.

“For in the place wherein the Highest beginneth to shew his city, there can no man’s building be able to stand.” When the Highest’s city comes, whatever is there has to go. That is why he said, I make all things new.

Read on into 55 and 56: “And therefore fear not, let not thine heart be affrighted, but go thy way in, and see the beauty and greatness of the building.” Y’all think you’ll be able to see up there into space? No. He is telling Ezra, look at this: can you see the top? Ezra can’t see the top, and he can’t even see from one side to the other, because it is 1,500 miles all around. “And then shalt thou hear as much as thine ears may comprehend.” The ears may not comprehend it, which is what 1 Corinthians 2:9 says. So this is different from Isaiah 60, where the nations build up our walls. Two different kingdoms.

Isaiah 60 and Revelation 21 are two different things. Isaiah 60 says the nations shall build: “And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls.” Look at the picture of the city 1,500 miles cubed: do y’all think the nations can do that? They cannot go into space and build that. This is two different kingdoms.

Why is this city so big? “Thus saith the Lord, The heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool.” Do y’all hear what he said? The heaven is his throne, the earth is his footstool. “Where is the house that ye build unto me?” Where is the house that you man, you Israelites, can build for him on earth? A city measured by the measure of an angel, rising out into space, is the house for the one whose throne is heaven.

“Howbeit the most High dwelleth not in temples made with hands; as saith the prophet, Heaven is my throne, and earth is my footstool: what house will ye build me? saith the Lord: or what is the place of my rest?”

That goes back to Isaiah 60, where the nations shall build up our walls. This ain’t talking about the same thing. This city is not made with hands; the pictures of it are only artist renditions.

“But as it is written, Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him.” That is what we just saw on the screen. When people read this in church they don’t know what it is really saying, and they have you thinking about something else. He has got that kingdom prepared for us; that is what this is talking about on this level. The ear that has not heard is Ezra’s “as much as thine ears may comprehend”.

“The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary.” Isaiah 60 has a sanctuary, built up and beautified. Revelation 21:22 says “I saw no temple therein.” So that is different: there will be no temple in the city, because the Father and the Son are the temple of it.

To further prove that verse 24 is a recap: “And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.” So there are no nations when this kingdom comes from heaven; there are no more nations. When Revelation 21:24 speaks of “the nations of them which are saved” and “the kings of the earth”, it is recapping the time of Revelation 20, before the end.

More proof. “The forces of the Gentiles shall come unto thee”: the word forces means wealth. The camels and “the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah; all they from Sheba shall come: they shall bring gold and incense”; the flocks of Kedar and the rams of Nebaioth minister; the ships of Tarshish bring Israel’s sons from far, “their silver and their gold with them”. “And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls, and their kings shall minister unto thee: for in my wrath I smote thee, but in my favour have I had mercy on thee. Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles, and that their kings may be brought.”

Back to Revelation 21:24-26: “the kings of the earth do bring their glory and honour into it”, “the gates of it shall not be shut at all by day”, “they shall bring the glory and honour of the nations into it.” That is saying the same thing we just read in Isaiah 60.

sense.text:
“He shewed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb.” Then “the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.” So the nations are here now. That means it is going back to chapter 20, back to Isaiah 60, back to Zechariah 14.

The tree of life “yielded her fruit every month”: yielding understanding every month. The leaves are for the healing of the nations, and that is the only way for the nations: they got to come up, like during the Feast of Tabernacles. You must come up, you must obey.

“And there shall be no more curse”: meaning Deuteronomy 28 is done; there is no more curse on us. “And they shall see his face; and his name shall be in their foreheads”: we are going to see the Lord’s face, and his name shall be in our minds. “And they shall reign for ever and ever.”
“Behold, I come quickly: blessed is he that keepeth the sayings of the prophecy of this book.” We got to keep the sayings of the prophecy of this book.

John fell down to worship before the feet of the angel. “Then saith he unto me, See thou do it not: for I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren the prophets.” Did anybody pick anything up in that? The angel said, I am your fellow servant, and I am of your brothers the prophets. Now that is some stuff right there. The angel is saying, don’t worship me, I am of your brothers the prophets; “worship God.”
“Seal not the sayings of the prophecy of this book: for the time is at hand.” Don’t seal it up.

Brothers and sisters, make sure you’re not unjust. “He that is unjust, let him be unjust still”: that means you can’t change. “He which is filthy, let him be filthy still”: if you are filthy of mind and heart and soul. “He that is righteous, let him be righteous still”: you brothers and sisters that are righteous, fighting in this truth. “He that is holy, let him be holy still.”

“My reward is with me, to give every man according as his work shall be.” He is going to give all of us according as our work shall be: whether you keep God’s law or you don’t keep his law. That is between every man and every woman; it’s on you, not on us. Some of you sit around saying you don’t want to do nothing in this truth, you don’t want to help build this truth: that’s on you.

“Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city.” That is the only way you enter the city.

“For without are dogs”: outside the gate. This is a recap to chapter 20, before the nations are destroyed. A dog: a shameless woman shall be counted as a dog (Ecclesiasticus 26:25), so if you are a shameless sister, don’t get mad. “And sorcerers”: you witches into horoscopes and juju beads and anal beads and whatever the hell you’re into. “And whoremongers”: you whoremonger brothers and sisters. “And murderers, and idolaters, and whosoever loveth and maketh a lie”: habitual liars, pathological liars.
“I am the root and the offspring of David”: Christ is telling us he comes out of King David’s lineage, and that he is the root and the offspring. That is heavy right there.

“And let him that is athirst come.” If you are thirsty for this truth, y’all better come. “Whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely”: Christ is that water of life. Take this truth freely.

“If any man shall take away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God shall take away his part out of the book of life, and out of the holy city.” The NIV takes away the words of the book. And you cherry-picking Christians out there: certain things you don’t want to deal with, you skip over.
“Surely I come quickly.” Christ said, I come quickly. “Even so, come, Lord Jesus.”

precepts.why:
The nations in Revelation 22 go back to Zechariah 14, about Egypt. “Every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.” “Whoso will not come up of all the families of the earth unto Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, even upon them shall be no rain”: that means death. “If the family of Egypt go not up”, there shall be the plague “wherewith the Lord will smite the heathen that come not up to keep the feast of tabernacles.”

That is the healing of the nations in Revelation 22:2: the only way for the nations is to come up and obey.

Zechariah 14 is saying the same thing as Isaiah 60: “For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish.” The nations that are healed in Revelation 22:2 are the nations that come up and serve; the ones that will not serve Israel perish.

The angel in Revelation 22:9 says he is “of thy brethren the prophets.” In Tobit the angel says the same: “I am Azarias, the son of Ananias the great, and of thy brethren.” And Tobit answers, “Thou art welcome, brother; be not now angry with me, because I have enquired to know thy tribe and thy family; for thou art my brother, of an honest and good stock: for I know Ananias and Jonathas, sons of that great Samaias, as we went together to Jerusalem to worship.” The angel says he is of their brethren, and Tobit receives him as a brother.

Then the angel reveals himself: “I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels, which present the prayers of the saints, and which go in and out before the glory of the Holy One.” They were both troubled and fell upon their faces, but he said, “Fear not, for it shall go well with you; praise God therefore.” “All these days I did appear unto you; but I did neither eat nor drink, but ye did see a vision.” “Now therefore give God thanks: for I go up to him that sent me; but write all things which are done in a book.”

So when he told them he was of the tribe of Naphtali, of their kin, the angel wasn’t lying at all. He knew exactly what he was talking about. That is the same angel speech as Revelation 22:9: I am thy fellowservant and of thy brethren; don’t worship me, worship God.

“And now, brother, behold what glory; and see the people that come from the east”, unto whom God gives for leaders Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and the prophets, down to “Zachary, and Malachy, which is called also an angel of the Lord.” What is Malachi called? An angel of the Lord. That means what it is saying. It is literal, it ain’t no hip talk. The angel in Revelation 22:9 told John what he is: of thy brethren the prophets.

If you are a dog, meaning what? “A shameless woman shall be counted as a dog.” That is what God says. So if you are a shameless sister, don’t get mad: Revelation 22:15 says “For without are dogs”, outside the gates of the city.

sense.text:
This ties up with what was just being said, and with what Deacon Malachi was saying. “For thou art blessed above many other, and art called with the Highest; and so are but few.” There are but few that will understand, that can comprehend and put these precepts together that are given from God, to explain them to the people. Not many people are going to understand this or could even explain it. You can give them all the precepts, but if the spirit of God is not on them, they won’t get it.

If you’re arguing about multiple wives and stuff like that, this ain’t for you. This is above your learning; you sit down here and you’re drowning in them precepts. So for those brothers out there listening: repent, get your mind right, so you can help spread this gospel and give the people the proper understanding, or just drown. We don’t have time to spend on multiple wives.
